keyTakeaways.headline: The data-centre gloom got a named rebuttal: HSBC Research and BNM say it is premature to price a Malaysian DC downturn from the US chip curbs - 3Q26 GDP grew 5.5%, private investment accelerated to 9.4%, BNM sees DC capex strong to 2030 and notes only about 13% of Malaysia's ~120 DC companies are Chinese
keyTakeaways.soWhat: After a weekend of three US pressure fronts (offshore-DC tax threat, BIS licensing rule, SEC Nvidia probe), the counter-case now rests on hard investment data rather than hope - boards should weigh both tracks rather than treating either as settled.

sectors.theme: After a weekend of three US pressure fronts on offshore AI infrastructure, HSBC Research and Bank Negara push back on the data-centre gloom: 3Q26 GDP held at 5.5%, private investment accelerated, and BNM sees DC capex strong to 2030 with only 13% of players Chinese

items.headline: HSBC Research and BNM say it is premature to price a Malaysian data-centre downturn from the US chip curbs - 3Q26 GDP grew 5.5% and private investment accelerated to 9.4%
items.detail: StarBiz's Monday lead (Nicole Chew, The Star) reports HSBC Global Investment Research arguing it is still premature to draw conclusions on how Washington's latest AI-chip curbs - imposed on data centres in four Asean countries including Malaysia - will hit the sector, noting businesses adapted after the Russia-Ukraine war, the 'Liberation Day' tariffs and the US-Iran war. The caution lands on 3Q26 GDP of 5.5% (announced Wednesday 18 Nov), with BNM data showing private investment up 9.4% (4.3% in 2Q26, 7.4% in 3Q25) and at 17.2% of GDP. BNM governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said DC investments should remain strong until at least 2030, and that of about 120 DC companies in Malaysia only 13% (about 17) are Chinese - the rest are from the US, Australia, Canada and Malaysia. Sunway University's Dr Yeah Kim Leng said the DC/AI share of private investment is likely substantial, with DC and AI projects accounting for 44% of approved investments in 1H26. (All per The Star's reporting; BNM remarks were made at Wednesday's 3Q26 GDP press conference.)
items.soWhat: The counter-narrative now has named institutional backing: the demand-risk story (Trump's offshore-DC tax threat, the BIS licensing rule, the SEC's Nvidia probe) met a same-weekend rebuttal built on hard investment data. For DC-exposed boards the honest read is that both are true at once - pipeline commitments are real and long-dated, while the policy overhang is unresolved. The 13%-Chinese-ownership figure is the quotable defence against a 'China proxy' framing.

sectors.theme: Berjaya Assets leans into foreign demand for Times Square 2: about 80% of its RM1m-plus units go to overseas buyers, Taiwan the largest source, and a Prince Court healthcare tie-up is aimed at second-home buyers

items.headline: Foreign buyers take about 80% of Berjaya Assets' larger Times Square 2 units - Taiwan is the biggest source market; project 62% sold at RM625m GDV
items.detail: Berjaya Assets Bhd CEO Tan Tee Ming told SunBiz (theSun, Monday) that overseas purchasers account for an estimated 80% of buyers in the larger residences at Times Square 2, its 629-unit, 41-storey freehold serviced-residence tower on Jalan Imbi next to Berjaya Times Square and Bukit Bintang City Centre. The project, launched in 2024 at a RM625 million GDV, had sold 392 of 629 units (62%) as at September 2026, with completion targeted by end-2027. Units above RM1 million target foreigners - Taiwan is the largest overseas market with more than half of foreign buyers, followed by Singapore, India and Hong Kong plus a smaller number from China - while the roughly half of units around 488 sq ft target Malaysians. Most foreign owners are expected to engage Kite, Berjaya's Airbnb operator, for short-term rental, and Tan said some Taiwanese buyers are hedging China-Taiwan geopolitical uncertainty. On Saturday Berjaya Property Bhd formalised a partnership with Prince Court Medical Centre giving eligible buyers at Times Square 2 and The Ritz-Carlton Residences healthcare privileges (also reported by EdgeProp on Saturday).
items.soWhat: KL city high-rise demand is being underwritten by foreign money - specifically Taiwanese second-home capital with a geopolitical hedge motive - rather than domestic owner-occupiers. That mix supports take-up now but ties project risk to MM2H-style policy settings and cross-strait sentiment; watch whether other Bukit Bintang-tier developers report the same buyer skew at launches.
